headline: Police uniforms change again: Bangladesh restores khaki pants after 20 years
summary: The government has reinstated khaki trousers and introduced dark blue and light olive shirts for different police units, reversing multiple changes from the last two decades.
details: The Bangladesh government has reinstated the use of khaki pants for police uniforms for the first time since 2004, according to a home ministry announcement on Thursday.
Under the new rules, district police and other units will wear dark blue shirts, while all metropolitan police units will be instructed to wear light olive shirts.
This latest change comes after a series of rapid uniform overhauls during the interim government's tenure, including a brief shift to 'iron grey' designs.
The Bangladesh Police Service Association had previously demanded a reversal of recent changes, stating that most officers opposed the design and were not consulted.
Khaki has long been associated with law enforcement in the Indian subcontinent, reflecting a legacy of British-era military attire.
Officials noted that approximately Tk 760 million has already been spent on uniform changes during the interim period, raising concerns over costs amid economic strain.
caption:
Khaki is back. Bangladesh Police are changing their uniforms again, bringing back a look from 20 years ago.

The Bangladesh government has reinstated the use of khaki pants for police uniforms for the first time since 2004, according to a home ministry announcement on Thursday.

Under the new rules, district police and other units will wear dark blue shirts, while all metropolitan police units will be instructed to wear light olive shirts.

This latest change comes after a series of rapid uniform overhauls during the interim government's tenure, including a brief shift to 'iron grey' designs.

The Bangladesh Police Service Association had previously demanded a reversal of recent changes, stating that most officers opposed the design and were not consulted.

Khaki has long been associated with law enforcement in the Indian subcontinent, reflecting a legacy of British-era military attire.

Officials noted that approximately Tk 760 million has already been spent on uniform changes during the interim period, raising concerns over costs amid economic strain.

headline_marked: BNP leader [[hacked and injured in Mohammadpur]] attack
headline: BNP leader hacked and injured in Mohammadpur attack
summary: Nurul Islam, senior joint general secretary of the BNP's Ward No. 33 unit, was attacked by men on motorcycles in front of his house.
details: A group of attackers on motorcycles hacked Nurul Islam, a 55-year-old BNP leader, in front of his house in Dhaka’s Mohammadpur area on Friday afternoon.
The victim, who serves as the senior joint general secretary of the BNP's Ward No. 33 unit, suffered serious injuries to his face, shoulder, and left hand.
According to Mohammadpur Police Station Inspector Rakibuzzaman Rakib, the attackers arrived on two bikes and stabbed the victim indiscriminately before fleeing the scene.
The incident occurred around 2:30 PM on Road No. 4 of Satmasjid Housing, shortly after Nurul Islam had returned from Friday prayers.
Locals rushed the injured leader to a local hospital and later to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where he is currently undergoing treatment.
Police believe the attack may have been motivated by political enmity, though they are working to identify and arrest those involved.
Nurul Islam, originally from Bhola, currently lives with his family in a rented house in Satmasjid Housing.
